ideas.name: AI Computing on Wasted Power
ideas.heading: AI Computing on Wasted Power: A Promising Business That’s Still Small
ideas.verdict: A Promising Business That’s Still Small
ideas.problem: Oil wells burn off gas, and wind and solar farms cut output when the grid is full.
ideas.does: Puts GPUs in containers there to run AI jobs that can pause.
ideas.why: AI jobs run on the cheapest power there is, without waiting for a grid connection.
ideas.kill: Each site is small and tied to one region’s wasted energy.
ideas.climate: It uses wind and solar power that would go to waste. Flared gas helps less, since the gas still burns.

ideas.name: Small Data Centers in Buildings with Spare Power
ideas.heading: Small Data Centers in Buildings with Spare Power: Investors Doubt Them, but Demand Exists
ideas.verdict: Investors Doubt Them, but Demand Exists
ideas.problem: Many buildings use only part of their grid connection.
ideas.does: Puts a few racks of GPUs in warehouses, factories, or stadiums.
ideas.why: Computing starts within months, on grid capacity a building already has.
ideas.kill: Earlier edge computing startups found too few customers, and scattered sites cost a lot to run.
ideas.climate: It uses existing grid connections instead of new lines and power plants.

ideas.name: Data Center Siting Maps
ideas.heading: Data Center Siting Maps: Plentiful yet Inadequate
ideas.problem: Developers buy land before the utility says how much power it can deliver.
ideas.does: Shows substations, spare grid capacity, gas lines, zoning, and water on one map.
ideas.why: Developers avoid buying land the grid can’t serve.
ideas.kill: Many companies already sell these maps, and only the utility knows what it has promised others.
ideas.climate: It steers new sites toward substations with real spare capacity.

ideas.name: Powered Land
ideas.heading: Powered Land: Buyers Will Pay a Premium, but to Developers They Already Trust
ideas.verdict: Buyers Will Pay a Premium, but to Developers They Already Trust
ideas.problem: Land the utility has agreed to power is scarce.
ideas.does: Options land near a substation, proves the utility can power it, then sells or leases it.
ideas.why: Buyers get land that can be powered soon, which saves them years.
ideas.view: A real business, but more real estate than tech
ideas.kill: Big buyers may build their own land teams, and towns may pause new data centers.
ideas.climate: It puts data centers where the grid already has room.

ideas.name: Brownfield Finder
ideas.heading: Brownfield Finder: Valuable Sites, but Developers Already Get More Offers Than They Can Use
ideas.verdict: Valuable Sites, but Developers Already Get More Offers Than They Can Use
ideas.problem: Closed power plants and factories can keep grid connections nobody uses.
ideas.does: Alerts developers when such a site closes.
ideas.why: Reusing an old connection could save a developer years of waiting.
ideas.kill: Developers already get more site offers than they can use, and old connections can’t always grow.
ideas.climate: It reuses existing grid connections instead of new power lines.

ideas.name: Phantom Request Filter
ideas.heading: Phantom Request Filter: Utilities Need It but Are Slow to Buy New Software
ideas.verdict: Utilities Need It but Are Slow to Buy New Software
ideas.problem: Developers apply at several substations for a data center they’ll build at only one.
ideas.does: Uses permits and contracts to estimate which queued projects will get built.
ideas.why: Utilities waste less time studying projects that won’t get built, so real ones connect sooner.
ideas.companies: None scores requests; [GridUnity](https://www.gridunity.com/) manages queues, and [Pearl Street](https://www.pearlstreettechnologies.com/) (now Enverus) and [piq Energy](https://www.piqenergy.com/) speed up studies
ideas.view: Depends on whether utilities buy it
ideas.kill: Utilities prefer cheap rule changes and buy software slowly, and their study vendors could add this feature.
ideas.climate: Utilities plan for real projects and build less that goes unused.

ideas.name: Batteries at Factories, Sold to Data Centers as Capacity
ideas.heading: Batteries at Factories, Sold to Data Centers as Capacity: My Top Idea, if FERC and Factory Owners Agree
ideas.verdict: My Top Idea, if FERC and Factory Owners Agree
ideas.problem: Big new data centers wait years to connect to the grid.
ideas.does: Puts batteries at businesses, which get rent and backup power; data centers buy the capacity, or pay factories to use less power.
ideas.why: Data centers connect years sooner, and hosts earn rent and get backup power.
ideas.companies: Voltus, [Xcel](https://www.xcelenergy.com/) with [Sparkfund](https://www.sparkfund.com/), [Base Power](https://www.basepowercompany.com/), [Outlast Power](https://outlastpower.com/), [Convergent Energy + Power](https://www.convergentep.com/), [Royal Powers Energy](https://rpenergyinc.com/)
ideas.view: My top idea, if FERC and factory owners agree
ideas.kill: FERC could reject PJM’s rule, and hosts may refuse the batteries.
ideas.climate: It adds batteries that store solar and wind power for the hours the grid needs it, or cuts factory use at the grid’s peak.

ideas.name: Data on How Big Data Centers Behave on the Grid
ideas.heading: Data on How Big Data Centers Behave on the Grid: Rules Would Make Owners Buy It, but Maybe Not from a Startup
ideas.verdict: Rules Would Make Owners Buy It, but Maybe Not from a Startup
ideas.problem: Utilities lack tested models of each big site.
ideas.does: Builds and tests the models, monitors each site, and writes compliance reports.
ideas.why: Big sites can show the utility they’re safe to connect, as new rules will require.
ideas.kill: NERC could narrow or delay its rules, and owners may use the models equipment makers already supply.
ideas.climate: Utilities connect big sites safely without building the grid for the worst case.

ideas.name: Software That Cuts Power When the Utility Asks
ideas.heading: Software That Cuts Power When the Utility Asks: Chips Now Cut Power Themselves, but Can’t Yet Deal with the Utility
ideas.verdict: Chips Now Cut Power Themselves, but Can’t Yet Deal with the Utility
ideas.problem: A utility can take years to serve a big data center’s peak.
ideas.does: When the utility asks, slows AI jobs that can wait, draws on batteries, and records the cut.
ideas.why: Data centers connect sooner by promising cuts they can reliably deliver.
ideas.view: Works while NVIDIA leaves utilities to partners
ideas.kill: NVIDIA’s DSX Flex could start taking requests straight from utilities.
ideas.climate: Data centers connect without new power plants built for the grid’s busiest hours.

ideas.name: Moving Tenants’ Jobs Between Colocation Buildings
ideas.heading: Moving Tenants’ Jobs Between Colocation Buildings: The Value Proposition Is Real, but Landlords Can’t Touch Their Tenants’ Computers
ideas.verdict: The Value Proposition Is Real, but Landlords Can’t Touch Their Tenants’ Computers
ideas.problem: A colocation building near its power limit can’t take AI tenants.
ideas.does: Moves some tenants’ jobs to another of the landlord’s buildings with spare power.
ideas.why: Landlords can take on more AI tenants without a bigger grid connection.
ideas.companies: None found; [Hammerhead AI](https://hammerheadco.ai/) adds its own racks instead; [Verrus](https://www.verrusdata.com/) offers “elastic power” leases
ideas.kill: Landlords can’t touch tenants’ computers, and buildings switch to batteries to cut grid use instead.
ideas.climate: It gets more computing from existing grid connections.

ideas.name: A Marketplace for Idle Computing
ideas.heading: A Marketplace for Idle Computing: Real Demand, Already Met by AI Companies’ Half-Price Batch Work
ideas.verdict: Real Demand, Already Met by AI Companies’ Half-Price Batch Work
ideas.problem: AI chips that answer live requests can sit partly idle overnight.
ideas.does: Sends jobs that can wait to idle chips.
ideas.why: Chip owners earn money from idle hours, and buyers pay less.
ideas.view: Mostly served; a small niche left
ideas.kill: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google already sell half-price batch work, and landlords own no chips to sell.
ideas.climate: Filling idle chips means fewer buildings and power plants built for daytime peaks.

ideas.name: Factory Capacity Finder
ideas.heading: Factory Capacity Finder: “Pure Gold” Data That Developers Gather Themselves
ideas.verdict: “Pure Gold” Data That Developers Gather Themselves
ideas.problem: Many factories use far less power than their grid connections allow.
ideas.does: Finds them in public data for battery developers.
ideas.why: Battery developers find good hosts quickly, without asking every utility.
ideas.kill: Battery developers find factories themselves, and PJM’s rule doesn’t require the capacity to be near the data center.
ideas.climate: Batteries go in at factories that are already wired, with no wait for new connections.

ideas.name: Hour-by-Hour Grid Planning
ideas.heading: Hour-by-Hour Grid Planning: The Software Exists, but Adoption Is Lagging and Data Is Missing
ideas.verdict: The Software Exists, but Adoption Is Lagging and Data Is Missing
ideas.problem: Many utility planners study only a few hours of the year, so they can’t count a site’s promise to cut.
ideas.does: Studies all 8,760 hours of the year.
ideas.why: Utilities can count a site’s promise to cut, and connect it sooner.
ideas.view: Software exists; adoption and data lag
ideas.kill: Few utilities use it yet, and they lack data on big data centers.
ideas.climate: Utilities build fewer lines and power plants for the busiest hours, when flexible sites cut back.

ideas.name: Construction Tracking
ideas.heading: Construction Tracking: Plenty of Tools Track Progress, Few Catch Clashing Drawings
ideas.verdict: Plenty of Tools Track Progress, Few Catch Clashing Drawings
ideas.problem: AI chip designs change mid-build, so crews tear out finished work.
ideas.does: Compares crews’ work with the design, and checks drawings for clashes before crews build.
ideas.why: Owners avoid tearing out finished work, and every day saved on a big site is worth millions.
ideas.view: Crowded for tracking, open for clash checks
ideas.kill: Procore or Autodesk could add AI that checks drawings for clashes.
ideas.climate: Less wasted material, and fewer delays.

ideas.name: Electrician Training and Hiring
ideas.heading: Electrician Training and Hiring: Room in Training, but Owners Don’t Hire the Crews
ideas.verdict: Room in Training, but Owners Don’t Hire the Crews
ideas.problem: A large AI data center needs thousands of electricians at once, often where few live.
ideas.does: Trains electricians on liquid cooling and high-voltage systems, and matches traveling crews to projects.
ideas.why: Projects finish sooner when enough skilled crews are available.
ideas.view: Weak as a marketplace; promising but unproven as training
ideas.kill: Contractors and unions control hiring, and factory-built modules cut the work done on site.
ideas.climate: Indirect: data centers get built faster.

ideas.name: Community Approval
ideas.heading: Community Approval: Developers Make Promises, but No One Checks Them Independently
ideas.verdict: Developers Make Promises, but No One Checks Them Independently
ideas.problem: More towns are blocking data centers, and can’t check a developer’s promises.
ideas.does: Helps developers win approval; a separate company checks they keep their promises.
ideas.why: Projects win approval sooner, and towns can trust what developers promise.
ideas.view: Intriguing, but depends on who pays
ideas.kill: Developers put their community budgets into staff, and no one yet requires an outside check.
ideas.climate: Towns accept projects from developers who keep their promises.

ideas.name: Operations Software for On-Site Power and Cooling
ideas.heading: Operations Software for On-Site Power and Cooling: A Crowded Field, Yet No One Runs the Whole Site
ideas.verdict: A Crowded Field, Yet No One Runs the Whole Site
ideas.problem: New campuses add power plants and liquid cooling from several suppliers, and small crews run it all.
ideas.does: Lets a small crew run all of it from one screen, within limits the operator sets.
ideas.why: A small crew can run a complex site safely, without juggling each maker’s tools.
ideas.kill: Equipment makers could ship tools that truly work with each other’s equipment.
ideas.climate: Sites run their batteries, cooling, and power plants better, even after the gas plants become backup.

ideas.name: Operations as a Service
ideas.heading: Operations as a Service: Real Demand, Lower Margins
ideas.problem: Data centers that build their own power plants must also run them.
ideas.does: Runs the plant under contract with its own crew, and carries the risk if it fails.
ideas.why: Data centers get on-site power without building a team to run it.
ideas.kill: Lower margins than software, and utilities or hyperscalers may run the plants themselves.
ideas.climate: Specialist crews run on-site power plants more efficiently.

ideas.name: Predicting Failures Across Small Sites
ideas.heading: Predicting Failures Across Small Sites: A Useful Feature, but Weak on Its Own
ideas.verdict: A Useful Feature, but Weak on Its Own
ideas.problem: Thousands of small AI sites can’t each have a technician on hand.
ideas.does: Predicts failures and sends a few technicians to the most urgent repairs first.
ideas.why: A few technicians can keep many small sites running.
ideas.companies: Vertiv and Schneider Electric, for their own equipment
ideas.view: Weak on its own; a feature of 6.1
ideas.kill: Big fleets of small sites may never appear, and equipment makers already predict failures.
ideas.climate: Fewer truck trips and less spare equipment.
